NEW DELHI: Amid concerns over deficiencies in quality of works and premature failures in expressways and NH projects, the road transport ministry will engage a third party inspection agency (TPIA) for inspection and examination of around 5,000 km of expressways and highway stretches from the start of construction until project completion. The agency’s technical personnel will conduct five inspection visits per stretch and will submit the report with recommendations for action.“Govt will bear the cost for such an exercise. NEW DELHI: Expressing concern that many engaging in the practice of dowry are not getting punished, Supreme Court has passed a series of directions to streamline and expedite trial in such cases.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih said there was a need for time-bound completion of trial in dowry cases and directed the high courts to periodically review pending criminal appeals.“Many who openly seek and give dowry go scot-free. It has been noted time and again, in various judicial pronouncements, that Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, suffers from various difficulties in its implementation. This Court further acknowledged that when it comes to the giving and taking of dowry in particular, this practice unfortunately has deep roots in society; hence, it being not a matter of swift change, a concentrated effort is needed on the part of all the involved parties, be it Legislature, Judiciary, law enforcement agencies, civil society organisations, etc,” the apex court said.It said that all trial courts shall endeavour, as far as is practicable and subject to compliance with statutory safeguards under CrPC/BNSS, to secure prompt appearance of the accused after the filing of a chargesheet, and thereafter, consider the framing of charges within 60 to 90 days.“Trial Courts/High Courts shall discourage unnecessary adjournments and ensure that adjournments are granted only after recording reasons in writing. Where counsel for the accused repeatedly remains absent without sufficient cause, appropriate Legal Aid Counsel or Amicus Curiae may be appointed to ensure that proceedings are not unnecessarily delayed. Additionally, where the Investigating Officer has been transferred or has retired, a substitute or holding officer shall be nominated sufficiently in advance to avoid adjournments,” it said.The bench also directed states/Union territories and high courts to conduct periodic training and sensitisation programmes for judicial officers, police officials, prosecutors, protection officers, counsellors through judicial academies, police training institutions and other appropriate bodies.
Article Summary: A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih said there was a need for time-bound completion of trial in dowry cases. All trial courts shall consider framing of charges within 60 to 90 days, the SC bench said.

Article Title: India’s petroleum products’ exports surge 8% in July
Article Text:
Govt data showed India exported 2.4 million tonnes (MT) of diesel in July this year.

NEW DELHI: India’s export of petroleum products recorded a year-on-year surge of over 8 percent in July, as margins improved amid a global supply shortage following Russia’s ban on diesel exports and ample supplies of crude to India during the US-Iran ceasefire.Govt data showed India exported 2.4 million tonnes (MT) of diesel in July this year, up from 2.2 MT in the corresponding month last year, while total petroleum product exports rose from 5 MT to 5.5 MT. Diesel is currently commanding nearly 70 percent premium over crude, making exports lucrative for refiners despite the windfall gains tax govt brought in to ensure adequate domestic stocks.While the Indian basket of crude averages $90 per barrel this month, diesel averages $150 per barrel. Windfall tax imposed by govt, however, has ensured refiners meet domestic demand before exporting the surplus.India is the second-largest crude importer, but it has stepped up fuel exports, consolidating its position as a major supplier of refined petroleum products to neighbouring countries as well as South Asian, African and European nations. Indian refiners import 40-45 percent of their crude requirements, but they export a significant part of refined products, with experts pointing out that they have also sent cargo of refined fuel to Russia, whose refining capacity has come down drastically because of damage from drone attacks by Ukraine.Russian refineries were processing around 3.8-3.9 million barrels per day (mbd) in July, down from 5.3 mbd a year ago, forcing the country to ban diesel exports and start importing.“A renewed wave of Ukrainian drone attacks since March, following a brief pause over the winter months, has significantly disrupted Russia’s refining system, pushing refinery runs to multi-decade lows of around 3.8 million barrels per day. Persistent attacks on refining infrastructure have tightened domestic product availability and prompted Russia to impose restrictions on exports of key fuels, including diesel, gasoline and jet fuel,” said Nikhil Dubey, lead analyst with Kpler.He added that cargoes of refined fuel from India, Turkey and Morocco have moved towards Russia. “Some Indian-origin cargo, such as volumes from Nayara Energy, have moved through traders and involved ship-to-ship (STS) transfers,” he added.According to S&P Global Commodities at Sea, India’s clean product exports, excluding LPG, averaged around 1.4 mbd in July and 1.1 mbd in Aug, with nearly 70 percent of volumes loaded from Sikka port, the key gateway for Reliance Industries’ Jamnagar refinery. Nayara Energy’s Vadinar refinery also emerged as a major exporter following its turnaround, supported by continued access to Russian crude.Abhishek Ranjan, Lead South Asia Fuels & Refining, S&P Global Energy, said that diesel exports became more profitable in July as the export tax fell by about $3 per barrel and profit margins rose 44 percent over the previous month, creating a strong incentive to ship more diesel overseas. Diesel accounted for roughly 43 percent of total exports, reflecting strong international demand for middle distillates and India’s ability to redirect cargo towards these markets.“Indian refiners were able to capture stronger margins and gain market share in export destinations despite broader global supply challenges,” Ranjan said.Analysts suggested that crude oil refining in West Asia, which catered to several African countries, has also declined by nearly 1.6 mbd from 2025 levels to about 8 mbd in 2026, opening an additional market for India.“East Africa, which has traditionally sourced a large share of its refined products from the Middle East, has seen those supply routes disrupted by constraints around the Strait of Hormuz and, more recently, the Bab el-Mandeb. The resulting supply gap has opened up additional outlets for Indian diesel, with refiners redirecting barrels towards African markets to replace some of the disrupted Middle Eastern supply,” Dubey said.
Article Summary: India exported 2.4 million tonnes (MT) of diesel in July this year, up from 2.2 MT in the corresponding month last year. Total petroleum product exports rose from 5 MT to 5.5 MT. Diesel is currently commanding nearly 70 percent premium over crude, making exports lucrative for refiners.

NEW DELHI: In the Centre’s first formal push to enforce compliance with Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act across the govt, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan has directed all central ministries, state govts and UT administrations to prepare time-bound implementation plans and appoint senior nodal officers to oversee compliance with the law.In a letter addressed to all secretaries at Centre and chief secretaries of states, Somanathan has asked them to accord high priority to the implementation of DPDP Act, stressing that the legislation is critical for protecting personal data and strengthening public trust in digital governance while enabling its lawful use.Somanathan has outlined steps, including identification of personal data processing activities and preparation of data inventories, review of consent and grievance-redressal mechanisms, establishment of governance structures, the strengthening of technical and organisational safeguards, review of contracts with third-party data processors, capacity building of officials and adoption of privacy-by-design principles in govt digital services.The communication noted that govt entities functioning as “data fiduciaries” under the Act are required to put in place measures for compliance. Ministries, departments and state govts have been asked to undertake a systematic review of their digital systems, data-processing practices and governance mechanisms.Somanathan said the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), the nodal ministry for the Act, has initiated guidance material supply, awareness campaigns, capacity-building programmes and stakeholder consultations to support its implementation.He has sought status reports on the law’s implementation so that common challenges can be addressed in a coordinated manner.

NEW DELHI: The Centre has identified 160 district hospitals for the first phase of a programme to increase emergency and trauma care capacity by 50%, with the facilities targeted for strengthening by March 2027, as the government moves to implement key health-sector announcements made in the Union Budget 2026-27.Union Health Minister J P Nadda reviewed the progress of the projects on Thursday and directed officials to ensure time-bound implementation, regular monitoring and coordination between ministries, states and institutions.A total of 613 district hospitals have been categorised for phased implementation after a gap analysis against Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS). An expert committee finalising the staffing structure has submitted its report.Mental healthcare was also reviewed, with NIMHANS-II planned as a 1,000-bed institute and CIP, Ranchi and LGBRIMH, Tezpur being upgraded as regional apex institutions. Article Title: India & China announce 8-point boundary consensus before Xi's visit, target early & substantial harvest in border delimitation

NEW DELHI: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question - co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi this week - had led to an 8-point consensus, signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month.These included advancing consultations for an "early and substantial harvest" of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, expanding trans-border trade and rivers cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the SR talks.Building upon the outcomes from the last round of talks in 2024, the 2 sides agreed that the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management would advance discussions on an “Early and Substantial Harvest” of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference, said the joint statement.India and China had agreed last year to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC), to explore early harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas.The formulation was changed to early and substantial on this occasion.Two additional meeting points for military talks and 2 more channels of border military hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed upon to reinforce border management measures, according to both sides.“The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution,” said the MEA in a statement. Unlike the Chinese readout of the talks on Tuesday, the joint statement did not mention package settlement or solution, although the 2005 agreement talks about making adjustments to reach a package settlement.The two sides also reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the guidance received from Modi and Xi, maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas and creating an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations.According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. “The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management,” said the joint statement.Both sides also noted the progress on trans-border cooperation, with the Indian side appreciating the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra (KMY) in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.“Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view to work together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas,” said the joint statement.India and China also agreed to hold the next meeting of the India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of the relevant MoUs. It’s important for India that China shares hydrological information during emergency situations based on humanitarian considerations. Article Summary: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question had led to an 8-point consensus. The consensus signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.
